description: The trust_law package advertises all-50-state coverage but stores static unverified doctrine and jurisdiction data without primary-authority verification metadata.
recommended_action: Contain current data as unverified research and create portal-native LegalAuthority, JurisdictionRule, and JurisdictionCoverage models before enabling production use.
acceptance_criteria: All existing static trust claims imported with verification_status='unverified' or quarantined
Every production rule links to primary authority
UI displays support level and human-review status

description: UCC filing assistant can generate financing-statement instructions without verified state filing-office rules or attachment/security-agreement gating.
recommended_action: Gate UCC outputs as draft educational analysis until official state rules and Article 9 requirements are modeled with human review.
acceptance_criteria: Filing instructions cannot be emitted as final advice
Attachment, value, rights in collateral, and authenticated security agreement checks exist
Official filing-office authority and last verified dates are stored
phase_2b_notes: Phase 2B adds evidence-based UCC filing assessment with attachment/security-agreement/value/debtor-rights gates for NY/PA/NJ, but legacy UCC assistant containment remains open.

description: Pseudo-legal/private-law claims are detected in one router but there is no durable quarantine model, source-ingestion class, or review workflow.
recommended_action: Implement a source-ingestion classifier and unsupported-claim quarantine with source links, evidence hashes, warnings, and no production rule promotion path without primary authority.
acceptance_criteria: UNVERIFIED_PRIVATE_LAW_CLAIM source class exists
Quarantined claims are tenant-scoped and auditable
Tests cover accepted-for-value, birth-certificate securities, secret Treasury account, tacit acquiescence, and immunity claims

description: No normalized creditor-response workspace exists for claimant identity, ownership chain, servicer/collector role, notices, deadlines, disputes, arbitration, court status, or evidence-readiness score.
recommended_action: Create creditor matter/evidence/deadline models and an explainable evidence-readiness score that does not rely on pseudo-legal terminology.
acceptance_criteria: Creditor evidence score factors and weights are transparent
Original-creditor versus debt-collector classification is modeled
Deadline and evidence preservation workflows are tested

description: No portal-native legal authority/rule schema exists with citation, source URL, effective date, repeal date, last verified date, verifier, verification status, limitations, and machine-readable rule logic.
recommended_action: Implement LegalAuthority and JurisdictionRule persistence under portal models with raw SQL migrations and tests.
acceptance_criteria: LegalAuthority model includes all directive-required metadata
JurisdictionRule model supports effective dates, exceptions, conflicts, confidence, and human-review flag
Tests cover current, repealed, future-effective, conflicting, and unverified rules
phase_2b_notes: Phase 2B generalizes governed jurisdiction packages and adds NY/PA legal-authority/rule records, but full portal persistence and all-state coverage remain incomplete.

description: No explainable trust health and resilience assessment engine exists for the required 25 score dimensions.
recommended_action: Create trust assessment models and scoring service with evidence links, missing evidence, authority references, limitations, and professional-review triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Every score exposes factors, weights, evidence, assumptions, limitations, and review triggers
UNKNOWN is used when evidence is insufficient
Tests cover missing evidence and conflicting jurisdiction facts

description: Financial features are dashboard/billing oriented and do not provide professional-grade ledgers, audit-style procedures, workpapers, or an audit-readiness binder.
recommended_action: Design separate accounting/audit-readiness models with clear NOT_AN_AUDIT labeling and CPA review workflow.
acceptance_criteria: General ledger and workpaper schemas exist
Outputs are labeled AUDIT-READINESS WORKPAPER PACKAGE - NOT AN INDEPENDENT AUDIT
Tests cover assertions, reconciliations, proposed adjustments, and reviewer notes

description: The portal has RBAC, audit, encryption, and storage primitives, but lacks integrated data classification, purpose-bound access, privacy budget, selective disclosure, honeytokens, retention/legal holds, and export controls for the proposed expansion.
recommended_action: Add privacy/security policy models before enabling high-volume legal/financial document exports.
acceptance_criteria: Data classification taxonomy exists server-side
Access purpose and export logging are enforced
Sensitive-field exposure is tracked and testable

description: Existing parliament functionality is static/demo/prototype and lacks durable queues, batch manifests, weighted evidence voting, dissent preservation, and 1,000-document processing.
recommended_action: Implement a portal-native parliament job architecture with idempotent tasks, document chunks, votes, dissents, conclusions, checkpoints, and deterministic test mode.
acceptance_criteria: Decision states include insufficient evidence, conflicting authority, superseded, and human review required
Dissent and minority reports are preserved
Synthetic 1,000-document run reports throughput, errors, retries, and recovery

description: Trust Law and AI Parliament screens use hard-coded demo data and do not show verification status, support status, authority links, professional-review gates, or evidence-weighted conclusions.
recommended_action: Move legal/parliament content behind APIs and display support level, verification status, limitations, and human-review state.
acceptance_criteria: UI no longer embeds legal rules as source constants
Every jurisdiction displays support status
Professional-review gates are visible and server-enforced
phase_2b_notes: Phase 2B adds NY/PA jurisdiction workspaces, Northeast comparison, and UCC assessment frontend routes with warnings, but legacy TrustLaw/AI Parliament demo surfaces remain hard-coded.

description: No test suite covers legal-rule effective dates, supersession, conflicting authority, unsupported-claim quarantine, creditor evidence scoring, trust simulations, privacy exports, or parliament scale.
recommended_action: Create focused unit, integration, E2E, security, and fixture tests before claiming feature completion.
acceptance_criteria: Legal-rule fixture set includes current, repealed, future, conflicting, nonuniform, incomplete, secondary-only, and unsupported claims
Security tests cover tenant boundaries and unauthorized export for new surfaces
Parliament scale test processes 1,000 synthetic documents
phase_2b_notes: Phase 2B adds focused regional rule, comparison, UCC assessment, API, frontend route, and containment tests, but broader proposed feature areas remain untested.

description: Many target domains for this expansion are excluded from active Ruff linting, including trust_law, parl, agent_protocol, financial_mastery, legal_intelligence, and artifacts.
recommended_action: Keep new production code in actively linted portal/web paths or explicitly add new paths to quality gates; avoid expanding excluded legacy modules as production authority.
acceptance_criteria: New production modules pass Ruff/Black or web lint/type-check
Legacy excluded modules are not used as production legal authority
CI scope is documented for the new feature

description: No effective-date, repeal-date, transition, and supersession engine exists for legal authorities or jurisdiction rules.
recommended_action: Model effective ranges and supersession links before any rule can be evaluated for a specific date.
acceptance_criteria: Rule lookup accepts an analysis date
Future-effective and repealed rules are not active for current analyses
Superseded rules remain queryable but inactive

description: The repository has conceptual conflict handling in Blackstone, but no portal workflow to record, expose, and resolve conflicting legal authority for production rules.
recommended_action: Create conflict records and require human review before a rule with unresolved controlling conflict is used as a conclusion.
acceptance_criteria: Conflicting authorities are linked to propositions and rules
Rule evaluation can return CONFLICTING_AUTHORITY
Review decisions preserve both supporting and opposing evidence

description: No production professional-review gate exists for legal rules, UCC outputs, trust clauses, creditor-response conclusions, tax conclusions, or audit-readiness findings.
recommended_action: Implement professional review items, reviewer roles, dispositions, expiry, and server-side enforcement before production eligibility.
acceptance_criteria: Rules cannot become HUMAN_REVIEWED without a review record
Execution-ready documents are blocked absent approved review
Review actions are audit logged and reversible only through supersession

description: No production-grade jurisdiction coverage exists; all fifty states, District of Columbia, and federal overlays are explicitly NOT_STARTED in Phase 0.
recommended_action: Use the coverage scaffold as the only support-status source until primary authority research advances individual jurisdictions.
acceptance_criteria: Coverage contains all required jurisdictions
No jurisdiction support status exceeds verified evidence
UI and APIs display support status

description: No source-ingestion pipeline classifies documents into the directive's authority, professional, client, educational, private-template, unsupported-claim, or unknown classes.
recommended_action: Add source document classification and verification metadata before migrating existing source material.
acceptance_criteria: Every ingested document has a source class
Authority weight and verification state are stored
Unsupported claims are classified separately from valid citations

description: Evidence hash and snapshot primitives exist, but legal rules, UI legal content, UCC summaries, and parliament conclusions do not yet require source provenance links.
recommended_action: Require source document IDs, content hashes, citation extraction metadata, and evidence links for every production rule and conclusion.
acceptance_criteria: Rule records cannot be activated without authority provenance
Parliament conclusions preserve supporting and opposing evidence
UI displays provenance summaries and limitations

description: Existing parliament demos use simple vote-style consensus and do not require mandatory dissent, minority reports, source-diversity checks, or unsupported-consensus detection.
recommended_action: Replace simple voting with weighted evidence disposition, mandatory dissent preservation, and human-review escalation for unsupported consensus.
acceptance_criteria: Every conclusion stores dissent and unresolved conflicts
Simple majority alone cannot produce ACCEPTED
Unsupported consensus is detected and escalated

description: Audit logging primitives exist, but no audit event taxonomy exists yet for proposed legal-rule reads, source imports, quarantines, professional reviews, privacy disclosures, exports, and parliament approvals.
recommended_action: Define and test audit events for every sensitive Phase 1+ workflow before enabling user access.
acceptance_criteria: Sensitive reads and exports create audit events
Quarantine and review status changes are audit logged
Audit tampering tests cover the new event classes

description: Existing portal tenant/RBAC tests are reusable, but the proposed legal intelligence, creditor, privacy, audit-readiness, and parliament surfaces do not yet exist and therefore have no tenant-boundary tests.
recommended_action: Add tenant-boundary and IDOR tests with each new API surface.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-tenant legal source access is blocked
Cross-tenant creditor and trust assessment access is blocked
Unauthorized export attempts are rejected and audited

description: The current product lacks a unified server-side boundary separating legal education, document organization, issue spotting, automated rule evaluation, and professional legal/accounting conclusions.
recommended_action: Create output classification and review gates so user-facing responses cannot impersonate legal, tax, accounting, audit, or filing opinions.
acceptance_criteria: Every output is classified by allowed purpose
Professional conclusions require review state
Disclaimers and server enforcement match output class

description: Core jurisdiction coverage data is hidden by a broad data/ ignore rule and would not be staged by default.
recommended_action: Force-add only data/jurisdictions/coverage.json for Phase 0 and avoid exposing unrelated ignored data directories.
acceptance_criteria: Only coverage.json is tracked from data/jurisdictions
No broad data/ unignore rule is introduced
Tracking decision is documented

description: No statutory drift or stale-source monitor exists to detect changed statutes, regulations, official forms, court decisions, or uniform-law amendments affecting encoded rules.
recommended_action: Design re-verification schedules, last-verified metadata, and proposed update records before any jurisdiction becomes production eligible.
acceptance_criteria: Every authority has last_verified_at and verifier
Rules can be flagged stale without deletion
Statutory drift creates proposed updates requiring review

description: Delaware DAPT and Connecticut CUTS rules present novel risks not found in NJ/NY/PA: federal bankruptcy override of DAPT (11 U.S.C. § 548), DAPT 'no direct benefit' ongoing litigation, Connecticut's explicit self-settled prohibition vs. Delaware DAPT, and CUTS nonuniform provisions requiring case-by-case review. These require licensed-attorney review before any production use.
recommended_action: Phase 3A rules are TESTED but not HUMAN_REVIEWED. DAPT and CUTS rules require licensed-attorney review before production eligibility. No DAPT or CUTS rule may advance to production without explicit attorney review and bankruptcy-risk disclosure.
acceptance_criteria: All DAPT rules are flagged HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED and blocked from production eligibility.
All CT self-settled prohibition rules are flagged HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED and blocked from production eligibility.
Bankruptcy override conflict records are present and visible in comparison output.
Licensed-attorney review records are entered for all DAPT and CUTS rules before any production advancement.
phase_3a_notes: Added in Phase 3A. DEF-0025 captures novel legal risks specific to Delaware DAPT and Connecticut CUTS that were not present in NJ/NY/PA.
